summary: The per-directory entry cap (16384) and the 64 KiB `release` cap bound each item but not a field or the aggregate: homes under a user-owned /opt/java each carrying a ~64 KiB release with one giant JAVA_VERSION made jvm hold the values twice (rows + compose_output): 4000 homes -> 500 MB RSS, both roots at cap ~4 GB, SIGKILL under a 1 GB limit; .NET 100 frameworks x 4000 versions -> 766 MB. Reproduced independently by cpp-safety (cs-1), who also showed a 256 B value clamp alone is insufficient. Fixed in af30d6e3a: WalkLimits (4096 rows, 1 MiB of row text, 65536 entries visited across all roots and levels, sticky `exhausted`, `row_cap`) plus a 256 B clamp on recognised release values (`field_oversized`), pinned by literal boundary tests. fjarvis LOW 4 (aggregate output unbounded) is the same defect.
trigger: a JVM/.NET root writable by a non-agent principal holding many homes with large release files
classification_rationale: I5(a): a reproducible unavailability (SIGKILL) on an ordinary dispatch path

summary: supported + zero rows was documented as "genuinely absent / none is installed" (README, both YAML definitions, comments; found as sg-3 by security-guardian and T3 by docs-writer, resolved by pd-5 and X-1 with the concrete trigger): openSUSE/SLES keep JVMs under /usr/lib64/jvm and Oracle-RPM installs under /usr/java, neither walked, so a host with Java read as none installed. Fixed in af30d6e3a/d9db2fca3: every claim now says "none found at the standard roots", the roots walked and NOT walked are named, and jvm walks /usr/lib64/jvm (measured on openSUSE Leap 15.6). /usr/java stays unwalked (no capture): documented, tracked in #4922.
trigger: a SUSE host (or an Oracle-RPM install) with Java: `status|jvm|supported|-`, zero rows
classification_rationale: the docs and status semantics claimed absence the walk cannot establish

summary: Distro OpenJDK 8 packages ship NO `release` file (Ubuntu 22.04 openjdk-8-*, Rocky 9 java-1.8.0-openjdk-*, Alpine 3.20 openjdk8-*): the walk silently dropped such a home, so a host with JDK 8 read supported + zero rows (with 8+11+21 installed only 11 and 21 listed). Fixed in af30d6e3a: a home with bin/java or jre/bin/java but no release is a row `jvm|unmodelled|-|<path>|-` plus `release_missing` (constrained); real-capture layouts of the three distros are fixtures.
trigger: OpenJDK 8 installed from the distro package
classification_rationale: the plugin advertised "which runtimes are installed" while dropping a whole common family

summary: No wall-clock bound on operator-mountable walks: on a real NFSv4 hard mount with the server killed, the production jvm walk sat in D state (rpc_wait_bit_killable) for 218 s and the agent ThreadPool shape blocked 203 s; each hung dispatch pins one of the 4-32 shared command workers (quarantine shares the pool: I5(b)); no timeout is ever surfaced. Fixed in af30d6e3a: a candidate root on, under or containing a network mount, read from /proc/self/mountinfo (new agents/shared/network_fstype.hpp deny-list), is never opened (`network_fs_skipped`); unreadable mountinfo is `mountinfo_unreadable`. Residuals (a hang on a local-disk-backed path, a network type the deny-list does not name, TOCTOU between scan and walk) are disclosed in the README; the general agent-core bounded-call seam is tracked in #4875 (real measurement after the fix: 37 ms with the server down, `network_fs_skipped`; a raw stat on the export blocked until SIGKILL).
trigger: a hard NFS/CIFS/FUSE/autofs mount holding /opt/java (or a dotnet root) whose server is down at dispatch
classification_rationale: I5(a)/(b): reproducible unavailability on an ordinary path, shared with quarantine dispatch

adjudication_rationale: sre (independent of the reporter unhappy-path and of the author): the class is not closable inside a plugin; accept the deferral only together with the agent-core bounded-call seam and an in-flight-age gauge (#4875); the deny-list additions and the disclosed residual are the plugin-side maximum.
summary: A deny-list by filesystem name cannot see a STACKED filesystem (an overlay, ecryptfs or loop device over a dead network mount reports its own local type), a network type it does not name, a bare `fuse` mount, or a stalled local block device: each pins one of the agent's shared command workers (verified on real kernels, e.g. a daemonless FUSE mount under /opt/java killed the walk at 8 s). No plugin-side fix exists; the durable fix is a bounded-call seam in agent core, tracked in #4875 (file-reading plugins have no execution deadline; related #3925, #4360). Done here: six names added to the shared list in Fixed in 379eba240 (gpfs, panfs, vboxsf, prl_fs, fuse.ceph-fuse, fuse.vmhgfs-fuse), two more in Fixed in 2dee569ca (vmhgfs, fuse.prl_fsd), and the residual is disclosed in README caveat 5, the routed-concern row and the header comments. sre also asked that #4875 gain an in-flight-age gauge (a hung run never completes, so no duration metric sees it). OPERATOR CONFIRMATION PENDING: the waiver is stated in the PR comment for the operator to accept.
trigger: a dead stacked or unlisted network mount under a candidate root
classification_rationale: I5(b) on a shared serialised path; unfixable in-plugin

summary: The SDK helper yuzu::util::sanitize_utf8 checks only lead and continuation byte counts, so overlong (C0 80), surrogate (ED A0 80) and out-of-range (F4 90 80 80, F5..) sequences pass through field_or_dash and protobuf rejects each in CommandResponse.output (real protobuf: 7 of 20 probes failed); reported independently by cpp-safety, security-guardian (sg8-2) and cpp-expert. The helper is pre-existing and shared by four plugins (installed_apps, msi_packages and vuln_scan carry private lax copies), and the defect is already tracked as #4864 (consolidate onto one strict helper), so the fix belongs in its own change: a tested RFC 3629 implementation (about 57 lines, boundary table, differential against protobuf) was written during this gate and is attached to #4864; it was held out of this PR for size. The README, the routed-concern row and the field_or_dash comment disclose the exception.
trigger: a planted file or directory name with an overlong or surrogate sequence
classification_rationale: pre-existing shared-helper defect newly reachable through the runtimes call site

summary: The streaming scan (the fix for UP-A) returned when an unfinished line exceeded 64 KiB, so a mountinfo line over 64 KiB (an overlay with more than ~265 long-path layers built with fsconfig lowerdir+: 300 layers = 74,790 bytes) ended the scan before a later network mount was read: a 465 KB real table with such lines followed by two hard NFSv4 mounts (server stopped) returned `network_fs_skipped` in 42 ms on the whole-file build and hung the round-2 build to the 20 s kill. Fixed in 2dee569ca: a line too long to keep is dropped and scanning resumes at its newline (`ok=false`, so `mountinfo_unreadable` is still recorded); pinned by a stream case with a mount starting exactly at a read boundary after the long line (the mutants that fail open, forget ok, or never resume are killed).

summary: The brief called dropping `pending.clear()` in the new skip logic output-equivalent; four reviewers (unhappy-path, security-guardian SG-R3-1, cpp-safety CS3-1, quality-engineer QE-R3-1) showed it is not: with a real overlay-shaped over-long line (its " - overlay" separator lies in the dropped prefix) before a network mount, the stale prefix glues onto the next line and swallows the mount (5,364 of 20,000 fuzz tables; a build without the clear hangs again on a real 199,749-byte table), while the suite stayed green because the test's long line was filler. Six mutants survived (resume at the read's last newline, resume one line late, no clear, clearing the mounts already read, production_config dropping partial mounts or hiding `mountinfo_unreadable`). The shipped code was correct (unhappy-path: 900k-case differential against an oracle, 0 mismatches). Fixed in 99dd72968: the stream case keeps a mount before a real overlay head and two after it (one in the read of its newline, one at the next boundary) and asserts the same set through scan_mounts and production_config; all six die.

summary: The new wiring case (and the existing config case) set and cleared the run_leg harness globals by hand, the shape of run_leg's g_leg_root: a throw inside the run would leave a dangling pointer for the next run (no reachable trigger). cpp-safety flagged it as new manual cleanup that could be a scope guard (a policy-floor candidate only if adjudicated).
